metadata.title: ProRL: Prolonged Reinforcement Learning Expands Reasoning Boundaries in Large Language Models

abstract: Recent advances in reasoning-centric language models have highlighted reinforcement learning (RL) as a promising method for aligning models with verifiable rewards. However, it remains contentious whether RL truly expands a model's reasoning capabilities or merely amplifies high-reward outputs already latent in the base model's distribution, and whether continually scaling up RL compute reliably leads to improved reasoning performance. In this work, we challenge prevailing assumptions by demonstrating that prolonged RL (ProRL) training can uncover novel reasoning strategies that are inaccessible to base models, even under extensive sampling. We introduce ProRL, a novel training methodology that incorporates KL divergence control, reference policy resetting, and a diverse suite of tasks. Our empirical analysis reveals that RL-trained models consistently outperform base models across a wide range of pass@k evaluations, including scenarios where base models fail entirely regardless of the number of attempts. We further show that reasoning boundary improvements correlates strongly with task competence of base model and training duration, suggesting that RL can explore and populate new regions of solution space over time. These findings offer new insights into the conditions under which RL meaningfully expands reasoning boundaries in language models and establish a foundation for future work on long-horizon RL for reasoning. We release model weights to support further research: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B

key_findings.claim: Prolonged RL (ProRL) training can uncover novel reasoning strategies that are inaccessible to base models, even under extensive sampling.
key_findings.context: Challenges prevailing assumption that RL merely amplifies high-reward outputs already latent in the base model distribution.

key_findings.claim: RL-trained models consistently outperform base models across a wide range of pass@k evaluations, including scenarios where base models fail entirely regardless of number of attempts.
key_findings.context: Evaluated across diverse task suite using pass@k metric to compare RL-trained vs. base model solution coverage.

key_findings.claim: Reasoning boundary improvements from RL training correlate strongly with both the task competence of the base model and training duration.
key_findings.context: Suggests that longer RL training progressively populates new regions of solution space, conditional on base model competence.

key_findings.claim: RL can explore and populate new regions of solution space over time, indicating that continually scaling RL compute can yield reasoning improvements.
key_findings.context: Addresses open question of whether scaling RL compute reliably leads to improved reasoning performance.

llm_extraction.methods_summary: ProRL is a training methodology for large language models that incorporates three key components: KL divergence control (to regularize deviation from a reference policy), reference policy resetting (to prevent policy collapse during prolonged training), and a diverse suite of tasks with verifiable rewards. The approach is evaluated empirically by comparing RL-trained models against base models using pass@k evaluations across multiple tasks, including tasks where base models achieve zero success rate.
llm_extraction.limitations: Only the abstract is available; full experimental details, ablation studies, and statistical analyses are not reported here. The released model is based on a 1.5B parameter Qwen architecture (Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B), and generalizability of findings to larger model scales or different base architectures is not established from the abstract alone. The abstract does not report effect sizes, confidence intervals, or specific benchmark scores. The claim of 'novel' reasoning strategies requires further empirical verification of what constitutes inaccessibility to the base model versus very low-probability outputs.

methodology_details.approach: Prolonged reinforcement learning (ProRL) with KL divergence control, reference policy resetting, and diverse verifiable-reward task suite applied to a 1.5B Qwen-based language model.

domain_specific_fields.benchmark: pass@k evaluations across diverse reasoning tasks
domain_specific_fields.training_technique: KL divergence control, reference policy resetting
